questions.prompt: 360 counts per output revolution, a 20 ms tick, 9 counts in one tick. Speed in rad/s, precision 0.01.
2000 counts per revolution and a 5 ms tick. Smallest nonzero speed in rad/s, precision 0.001.
A shaft turns at 31.4159 rad/s. Speed in rpm, tolerance 0.5.
With a fixed encoder, what happens to the speed quantum 2*pi/(N*T) when the loop rate is raised from 100 Hz to 1 kHz?
options: It becomes ten times smaller, so the estimate is smoother and less noisy.
Ten times larger: one count now means more speed.
It does not change, because it only depends on the counts per revolution N.
It becomes zero because the loop is faster than the motor.
questions.explanation: T is ten times smaller, so one count per tick corresponds to ten times more speed. Faster is not better for counting; filter, use more counts, or measure the period.

questions.prompt: A speed filter y += alpha*(x - y) with alpha = 0.25 runs at T = 0.02 s. Approximate time constant T*(1-alpha)/alpha in seconds, precision 0.001.
With the clamp (conditional integration) rule, when may the integral state change?
options: Never while the output is nonzero or the motor is moving.
Only when the error is exactly zero at the sample instant.
Always, but with a gain reduced to one tenth.
When u is unsaturated, or the error pulls it back into range.
questions.skillLabel: PI loop with clamp and anti-windup
questions.explanation: The integrator updates if u equals u_raw, or if the saturated output and the error have opposite sense (the error would unwind it). Otherwise it holds.

questions.prompt: Kp = 0.2, Ki = 2, dt = 0.05, umax = 1. Setpoint 4, measured 1, integral state 0.3. Output u after clamping, precision 0.001.
questions.skillLabel: PI loop with clamp and anti-windup

questions.prompt: Same tick as the previous question, with the clamp rule. What is the integral state afterwards, precision 0.001?
questions.skillLabel: PI loop with clamp and anti-windup
questions.explanation: u_raw (1.2) exceeds the limit and the error (3) is positive, pushing further: the integrator holds at 0.3.

questions.prompt: The setpoint drops from an unreachable value to 10 rad/s, but the PWM stays at 255 for seconds. What is the likely cause?
options: Integrator windup: stored integral still saturates u.
The encoder wiring is loose or the A and B channels are swapped.
The dead zone compensation is set too small for this motor.
The PWM frequency is too high for the driver to follow.
questions.skillLabel: PI loop with clamp and anti-windup
questions.explanation: A PWM column stuck at full scale after the error changed sign is the signature of an unclamped integral.

questions.prompt: Dead zone 30 of 255, controller output u = -0.25. Signed duty (round to an integer).
Why add the dead-zone offset when mapping u to the duty?
options: To make the PWM frequency audible to the user.
To increase the supply voltage seen by the motor.
Duty below the stiction threshold moves nothing, so the integrator winds up.
To invert the direction.
questions.explanation: Below the stiction duty the motor stays still; mapping u to start at the dead-zone edge makes the loop gain roughly linear.

questions.prompt: A robot at 0.4 m/s keeps driving until a 250 ms command timeout fires. Distance travelled in metres, precision 0.001.
Which condition best defines a stall that the firmware should latch as a fault?
options: Speed above the setpoint for a single tick of the loop.
High duty with almost no speed for a sustained time.
Any change of direction.
A step response that shows 5 % overshoot at the peak.
questions.explanation: A blocked shaft or a dead encoder shows as a large drive with no motion for longer than the normal acceleration time.

questions.prompt: A step test gives K = 25 rad/s per unit of u and tau = 0.3 s. Lambda-tuned Kp for tau_c = 0.2 s (Kp = tau/(K tau_c)), precision 0.001.
Describe how you would run and read a step test of a speed loop, and which numbers you would report.
rubric: Applies a step in setpoint from rest, logs time, setpoint, estimated speed and PWM at the fixed rate (CSV over Serial).
Computes rise time (10-90 %), overshoot, steady-state error from the final samples and settling time into a 2 % band.
Looks at the PWM trace for saturation or windup and tunes in order: feed-forward and Kp, then Ki, reducing Ki if overshoot is too high.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Write the skeleton of the firmware loop: a timer sets a flag, the loop reads the encoder count once, estimates speed, runs a clamped PI, maps to PWM and checks a command timeout.
rubric: Timer interrupt only sets a flag; one loop iteration per tick with a fixed dt (no delay or blocking Serial inside).
Reads the count once per tick, computes speed in rad/s from the difference and the counts per revolution, optionally filters it.
Runs the PI with clamp and conditional integration, maps u to signed duty with the dead zone, and forces zero output (and integrator reset) when the command timeout expires.
questions.skillLabel: PI loop with clamp and anti-windup
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
